title: Responsive Design
summary: Responsive design adapts layout, content and interaction to available space, input and zoom—not device names alone; meet WCAG 2.2 AA SC 1.4.10 reflow at 320 CSS px.

MUST.text: Choose breakpoints where the current layout fails; test narrow widths, zoom and orientation.
Meet WCAG 2.2 AA SC 1.4.10 Reflow: content reflows without two-dimensional scrolling at 320 CSS px width (equivalent to 400% zoom at 1280 CSS px).

SHOULD.text: Preserve task priority and content order across widths.
Use fluid grids, relative units and max-width so content adapts without horizontal scroll.

AVOID.text: Do not shrink desktop columns until text and controls become unusable.
Do not rely on device-name breakpoints or horizontal scrolling for core tasks.

EXAMPLE.good: "Settings page reflows from two columns to one ordered column at 320 CSS px with no horizontal scroll."
EXAMPLE.bad: "Desktop table shrinks to 8px text and requires sideways scrolling to read."

FAILURE_MODES: Fixed-width containers cause two-dimensional scrolling at 320 CSS px.
Content order changes across widths hide primary tasks.
Breakpoints chosen by device names break on in-between sizes.
Zoom to 400% reveals clipped or overlapping controls.

checks.text: Reflows at 320 CSS px without 2D scroll?
